spec.name: dependency-waves
spec.intent:
Census: complete-persona-launch of plan persona-owned-enforcement, source commit a327bd6e96f3c92d1dba0242bf886e6abc094cda. The line at d8701e45 changes only planning/design/notebook records relative to that source; the original source census still applies. The prior implementer's isolated edits are unaccepted and are not a baseline. Use a fresh isolated checkout off the line after predecessors are whole. Do not run builds/tests/linters/formatters mid-flight; main/integrator verifies the coherent unit against only its criteria. No design changes or rubric redesign are authorized.

Realize the newly handed planner role rule in the authored planning skill and planner role surface: dependencies or shared outputs may require a singleton wave; do not call that a bad cut or pad it with unchanged work. Remove the universal singleton-nonterminal-wave rejection, while retaining dependency ordering, no concurrent output/reference contention, per-dispatch capacity, factor-based splitting and proportionate acceptance. Keep the wave recurrence and lifecycle vocabulary unchanged. This is a wording/law correction, not a runtime scheduling feature: existing plan wave computation already represents serial dependencies. Update the focused test and package release note. Do not edit the host-installed skills or historical plan/design records.
accept: A focused test over the authored plan skill and planner role rejects the old unconditional singleton-wave prohibition and requires the replacement to permit serial work for real dependencies/shared outputs without permitting concurrent contention or fake units. It must fail against the pre-change skill, not merely assert that a new test exists.

The existing wave recurrence, unit/plan lifecycle values, total realization/pin rules and capacity/acceptance constraints are unchanged. Inspection plus the focused canon test and existing formal-block/symbol checks are sufficient; no native harness or model run is owed for this wording unit.
